cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). They wrote to him about some matters, and now he's taking up the matters they wrote about. His opening line: "It is good to abstain from sexual relations."

cards.question: Paul says it's good to abstain from sexual relations. But because there is so much sexual immorality, what does he say each man and each woman should have?

answers.text: An elder to watch over them

cards.text: Next Paul brings up something in marriage he calls marital duty.

cards.question: Paul says only the husband should fulfill his marital duty, not the wife.
Paul says the husband has authority over his wife's body, and likewise the wife has authority over her husband's body.
Paul tells married couples not to deprive each other, with one exception. What is it?

answers.text: By mutual consent for a time of prayer
When one of them is away on a journey
During the days of a feast

cards.question: Paul says a married couple who stop for a time of prayer should come together again, so that ___ will not tempt them.
Paul adds a note about what he's just said: he says it as a command.

cards.text: Then Paul gets personal: "I wish that all men were as I am." Friend, if I ever wished that about myself, this whole bakery would be full of MUSTACHES.

cards.question: Paul wishes all men were as he is. But he says each man has his own ___ from God.

cards.text: Paul's working through it one group at a time, like me checking off a recipe card line by line. Next up: the unmarried and widows.

cards.question: What does Paul say is good for the unmarried and widows?

answers.text: To remain unmarried as he is
To marry as soon as they can
To move back with their families

cards.question: Paul says that even if the unmarried and widows cannot control themselves, they should still stay unmarried.

cards.text: Paul's line on it: "For it is better to marry than to burn with passion." Next, he turns to the married, and he says this command is not from him but from the Lord.

cards.question: Paul gives the married a command from the Lord. What does it say about a wife?

answers.text: She must not separate from her husband
She must pray for her husband daily
She must keep her husband's customs

cards.question: And if a wife does separate from her husband, Paul gives her two options. What are they?

answers.text: Stay unmarried or be reconciled to him
Remarry or go back to her family
Wait a year or ask the elders

cards.question: Paul says the husband has a command here too: he must not divorce his wife.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to the rest, and he labels this part right up front, like a sticker on a cookie box: "I, not the Lord". It's for a brother or a sister who's married to someone who doesn't believe.

cards.question: A believer's spouse doesn't believe, but is willing to live with them. What does Paul say the believer must do?

answers.text: Wait for them to believe first
Bring the matter to the elders

cards.text: Paul gives a reason for staying: the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife through her believing husband.

cards.question: When one spouse believes and the other doesn't, Paul says their children are holy, not unclean.

cards.text: Now the other side of it, friend. Paul's word to stay was for a spouse willing to live with the believer, so what if the unbelieving spouse leaves?

cards.question: If the unbelieving spouse leaves, Paul says the believer must follow them until they come back.
If the unbelieving spouse leaves, Paul says to let them go. In such cases, he says, the believing brother or sister is not ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "God has called you to live in peace." I think that line is a gift to anyone who's been through this one.

cards.question: Paul asks a believing wife and a believing husband married to unbelievers the same kind of question. What is it?

answers.text: How do you know whether you'll save your spouse
Have you prayed for your spouse today
Will your spouse join you at church

cards.text: Now Paul zooms out from marriage to EVERYBODY. Each one should lead the life the Lord has assigned to him, the one God has called him to.

cards.question: Paul says leading the life God called you to is something he prescribes only for the church in Corinth.

cards.text: ALL the churches, friend. Same recipe in every kitchen, no special batch just for Corinth.

cards.question: A man was already circumcised when God called him. What does Paul say he should do about it?
If a man was still uncircumcised when God called him, Paul says he should get circumcised.
Paul says, "Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing." Then he says keeping God's ___ is what counts.

cards.text: Paul sums it up: each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called. Then he gets to a harder case, someone who was a slave when God called him.

cards.question: What does Paul tell someone who was a slave when God called him?

answers.text: Don't let it concern you but take freedom if you can
Run away from your master as soon as you can
Stay a slave even if you're offered your freedom

cards.question: Paul flips things around. He says the one who was a slave when called by the Lord is the Lord's ___.
Paul says the one who was a free man when he was called is Christ's slave.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men."

And Paul lands it one more time: "Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him." But friend, Paul's still got plenty to say about marriage, and this conversation is NOT over.
